subject: BetaHealth — Data processing terms, subprocessor carve-outs & signing plan
messages:
From: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@betahealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Procure <sarah.proc@betahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BetaHealth DPA redline and a couple of clarifying Qs

Hi Neha / Rishi,

Attached is BetaHealth's first-pass redline on Redwood's DPA (see BetaHealth_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). A few quick items we flagged up-front:
- Subprocessor carve-out language: we need clarity on how Redwood will notify customers when a new subprocessor is added and whether limited carve-outs for analytics providers are possible.
- Cross-border transfers: BetaHealth operates in EU and CA; counsel asked whether Redwood will rely on SCCs, EU-US Addendum, or an alternative transfer mechanism.
- Evidence: procurement wants a short list of compliance evidence (SOC 2 scope & date, penetration test summary, breach notification SLAs).

Can you confirm how you'd like to proceed on the transfer mechanism and whether you can accept the carve-out language in §4.2? Also indicate the preferred signing route — DocuSign vs AdobeSign — and whether you can provide an initial execution timeline.

Thanks — looking to get procurement and counsel comfortable before we move to terms.

Tom Hayes
Head of Procurement, BetaHealth
Tom.Hayes@betahealth.com
Attachment: BetaHealth_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx, 84KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@betahealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BetaHealth DPA redline and a couple of clarifying Qs

Tom — thanks for the redline and the clear summary. Looping in Grace (privacy counsel) and Rishi (sales lead) for the DPA/legal path and procurement cadence.

Quick answers and flags from Redwood:  
- Subprocessor notifications: our standard process is a 30-day advance notice for routine subprocessors and immediate notice for any security-critical changes. We're open to a short carve-out for vendor analytics if BetaHealth provides a list of required controls; Grace, please see note below.
- Transfer mechanism: we typically execute SCCs for EU data and an EU-US Transfer Addendum for US-bound processing; where customers require an addendum or bespoke clause, we can append a Transfer Annex. If BetaHealth prefers SCCs only, we can propose SCCs + our standard Supplement.
- Evidence: we can provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), penetration test summary, and our incident response SLA. Rishi — I'll attach a one-page evidence checklist to share with procurement.

Proposed next steps: 1) Grace to comment on the redlines (by EOD 10/02), 2) Redwood will produce a response matrix and suggested language (target 10/03), 3) if agreeable, we can route for signature via DocuSign (preferred for our legal ops) and aim for execution week of 10/12. If BetaHealth requires AdobeSign, confirm and we'll switch.

I'll attach a short response matrix to this thread.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_Response_Matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 24KB)

Cc: Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@betahealth.com>, Sarah Procure <sarah.proc@betahealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BetaHealth DPA redline and a couple of clarifying Qs

Neha — thanks for the quick reply and the response matrix. I've attached counsel's annotated PDF with inline questions (Counsel_Annotated_Comments.pdf). A few clarifications for Redwood's team:

1) KMS / customer-managed keys: BetaHealth's security team prefers customer-held keys for certain PHI contexts. Is Redwood able to support a KMS/HSM integration, or provide encryption-at-rest with a customer BYOK option? If not, we'll need more robust compensating controls.

2) Subprocessor carve-out: counsel is open to a limited analytics vendor carve-out but needs (a) a published subprocessor list updated weekly and (b) a 14-day objection window rather than 30 for high-risk processors.

3) Transfers & SCCs: counsel prefers the SCCs approach for EU processing. If Redwood will rely on SCCs, please confirm which modules (Controller-Processor standard contractual clauses) and whether you propose any additional safeguards (e.g., contractual transfer annex).

4) SOC 2 evidence: please confirm the SOC 2 date and whether Redwood will execute an NDA prior to sharing the full report. Procurement would like a redacted copy first.

We have a procurement cutover date the week of 10/18; ideally the commercial and legal terms are agreed by 10/12 so that operations can schedule onboarding.

Emily Zhang
Senior Counsel, BetaHealth
emily.zhang@betahealth.com
Attachment: Counsel_Annotated_Comments.pdf (pdf, 75KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@betahealth.com>, Tom Hayes <tom.hayes@betahealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BetaHealth DPA — next steps and signature route

Emily / Tom — thanks for the detailed comments. Quick consolidated response and proposed path to execution: 

- KMS/BYOK: Redwood's platform supports customer-managed keys on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted API customers we offer BYOK for encryption-at-rest via our KMS integrations on a case-by-case basis; we'd be happy to confirm feasibility for BetaHealth and document controls. Grace — can you confirm standard language to offer (we propose a short clause: "Customer may use a customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest where Redwood's Dedicated or Private deployment is used")?

- Subprocessor notification & objection window: we can tighten the objection window to 14 days for processors flagged as "high risk" and we can publish a near-real-time subprocessor registry. We'll agree to the 14-day window for high-risk processors; routine subprocessors will maintain a 30-day notice.

- SCCs & transfer safeguards: Redwood will adopt the Controller-Processor SCCs (Module Two / Processor clauses) for EU transfers and will append a Transfer Annex summarizing technical safeguards (encryption, access controls, logging).

- SOC 2 evidence: we can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report under an NDA; procurement can sign the linked NDA (see HubSpot attachment) and we'll provide the redacted report within 2 business days of execution.

Execution plan: Redwood prefers DocuSign for the signature route (our legal ops already has automation in place). We will prepare a final response matrix and a consolidated DPA (round 2) by 10/08 and circulate for review. If BetaHealth confirms DocuSign, we'll open an envelope and propose a primary signer (BetaHealth procurement) and countersign path for Redwood.

Next steps for BetaHealth: confirm 1) KMS requirement (Yes / No / Only on Dedicated), 2) signature platform (DocuSign / AdobeSign), and 3) whether we should proceed with SCCs + Transfer Annex. If you confirm by 10/07, we should meet your 10/12 agreement target.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
